column1: # The second golden library's text queries (Kenney's CC0 game audio): what a developer would type, and what a right answer is.
# Columns (tab-separated, in this order, header required):
#   class        the class whose members are the right answers (golden/kenney/labels.csv), or `-` for a query that should find NOTHING
#   description  the words a person types. This file is the MAINTAINER'S wording: written with the class list in view, so it may use a
#                class's own words. `queries-paraphrase.tsv` asks for the same classes without them
#   rationale    one line: which files are the right answers and why, or what the nearest confound is
# **Written before the model had run on this library.** The class list, the manifest and both query files were committed first (the commit is
# `golden: the second library's labels and queries, frozen before the model ran`); every later change is a new row, never an edit, because a
# recorded number is about the old question. The expected confounds named in the no-answer rows are guesses made at the same time.
# A positive query's right answers are **every** file of its class. A class is the *author's own file names, grouped* — never a listener's
# judgement of what a sound is — so a label is only as good as Kenney's naming, and a confusable pair (`laser`, `phaser`, `electric_zap`)
# is a pair a developer browsing the pack would see too. `docs/guide/golden-set.md` has the whole procedure.
